design: Groundwater consumed by biopsy-proven CKDu patients
finding: >88% of samples showed excess hardness; 44% had F above 0.60 mg/L

design: 63 samples, 19 from wells used by CKDu patients
finding: Significantly higher pH, total hardness, EC, Ca, Mg, F, Cl, PO4 and SO4 in patients' wells

study: Duke / Ferguson lab 2023 (Environ Sci Technol Lett)
location: Rural Sri Lanka endemic vs non-endemic
finding: Glyphosate detected in 44% of endemic vs 8% of non-endemic wells; fluoride detected in 99% vs 80%; glyphosate, fluoride, hardness and vanadium positively associated with CKDu prevalence
Only 3.8% (wet) and 2.6% (dry) of samples were WQI excellent; 28.2% (wet) and 30.3% (dry) classed poor (WQI 100-200)
Over 60% of shallow wells had F above 0.6 mg/L; no evidence of heavy metals above detection limits; authors state data are insufficient to prove chemistry-CKDu link
By 2018 only 35% of households used untreated groundwater for drinking/cooking; about 50% used reverse-osmosis treated water
